topic.title_he: סופר את הימים עד יום ההולדת
topic.reason: הנושא נקבע בתוכנית החודשית (החבילה החודשית של 1 בנובמבר 2026, חריץ 3) ואין כאן טענה על תאריך בלוח השנה. ילדים בני 4 עד 5 שואלים כל בוקר כמה ימים נשארו, וקשה להם לדמיין זמן. מקורות שנקראו היום: Brightly (מורה לגן וחובה על לוח שנה שילדים בונים) ואת Empowered Parents (מושג הזמן אצל גיל הגן). בקטלוג יש ספר יום הולדת לגילאי 3 עד 8 (נבדק באתר היום), לשימוש פנימי בקישור בלבד.

sources.title: Tips, Tricks, and Books for Helping Kids Understand Calendars
sources.publisher: Brightly (Penguin Random House), written by a kindergarten and preschool teacher
sources.quote: Kids are more likely to internalize calendar concepts and patterns when they can put them in the context of their own lives. ... Challenge yourself to greet children each day with, “Happy Tuesday! On Tuesdays we _____!” ... Let the kids add cues to the calendar, like houses on no-school days, pizza slices for pizza lunch days, or Xs for days gone by, to give purpose and meaning. ... Ask them to point to “yesterday, today, and tomorrow,” find specific day numbers, or count the days or weeks until a significant event. ... Pairing movement with a song or chant can help the words stick
sources.supports: Kids make sense of calendar words through their own lives; a calendar kids add cues to (Xs for days gone by); counting the days or weeks to an event; songs and chants with movement; a greeting that names what we do each day. A teacher's practical article, not a clinical guideline.

sources.title: Teaching the Concept of Time to Preschoolers
sources.publisher: Empowered Parents (early years educators' parenting site)
sources.quote: Because time is an abstract concept, children need multiple opportunities to experience and understand it. ... Your birthday is in 2 weeks' time. ... Give them five minutes to tidy the class to understand how long five minutes feels ... Visual timers let kids watch the numbers count down. For young kids, 3 to 5 minutes is long enough. ... Predictable routines not only teach kids about time but also help them feel secure and safe. ... Create a poster with your kids that outlines the day's major activities. ... Baking and cooking with kids is a great opportunity for teaching them about how we use time when cooking, and it also gives them a feel for the passing of time.
sources.supports: Time is abstract and kids need repeated experiences of it; saying time words in context (a birthday in 2 weeks); feeling how long five minutes is; a visual timer for 3 to 5 minutes; a predictable routine and a routine poster; baking as a feel for passing time. An educators' site, used as general advice.

sources.title: Social Development in Preschoolers: Learning How to Share & Cooperate
sources.publisher: HealthyChildren.org, American Academy of Pediatrics (last updated 12/5/2024)
sources.quote: Three-year-olds are able to work out solutions to disputes by taking turns or trading toys. However, particularly in the beginning, you'll need to encourage this cooperation. ... Say to your child "use your words" to deal with problems instead of acting out. ... Remind them that when two children are sharing a toy, each gets an equal turn. ... Suggest ways to reach a simple solution when your child and another child want the same toy. They might draw for the first turn, for example, or find another toy or activity. ... Help your child with the appropriate words to describe their feelings and desires so that they don't feel frustrated.
sources.supports: Preschoolers can learn to take turns and trade toys but need encouragement at first; use your words; an equal turn for each child; draw for the first turn or find another toy; words for feelings. AAP page adapted from Caring for Your Baby and Young Child.

sources.title: Getting Preschoolers to Share…How Do You Do It?
sources.publisher: Pathways.org (pediatric therapists' nonprofit, last updated 18 Jul 2025)
sources.quote: In preschool years, children are still learning how to share, so it is okay if your child isn’t great at this skill yet. ... Something visual, like a timer, will let children know exactly when it’s time for them to give up a certain toy. ... explain that they can have a turn next ... point out how nice it was that Dad shared his water with Mom. ... Talk about how it would feel if they went to a friend’s house and wasn’t allowed to play with any toys. ... If your child has a toy that is their absolute favorite that they do not want to share, put it away before the play date!
sources.supports: Preschoolers are still learning to share; a visual timer shows when to give up a toy; explain they can have a turn next; point out sharing you see; talk about how it feels before a playdate; put away one absolute favorite toy. A nonprofit of pediatric therapists, used as general advice.

הדינוזאור הירוק שלי.
זה שאני ישן איתו.
אני רואה את היד שלו מתקרבת,
והלב שלי מתחיל לדפוק.

״רון, תן לו גם!״
אתם אומרים את זה ביחד,
ואני שומע רק דבר אחד:
לוקחים לי.
אז אני מחזיק חזק יותר,
ומסובב את הגב.

החבר מתחיל לבכות
מה אתם רואים:
ילד שלא מוכן לתת כלום.
מה קורה לי בפנים:
אני לא יודע אם הדינוזאור
יחזור אליי.

אמא מביאה שעון חול
שעון חול קטן על השטיח.
אני רואה את החול יורד.
מה יעזור לי לשמוע:
״חמש דקות לו, ואז הוא חוזר אליך.״

אני נותן, ולא מוריד עיניים
החבר מחזיק את הדינוזאור שלי.
אני יושב ממש לידו,
וסופר עם החול.
זה קשה. זה ממש קשה.
אבל אני יודע שהתור שלי בא.

אני כועס, ואומר את זה
במקום לחטוף, אני אומר:
״אני כועס! הוא שלי!״
מה יעזור לי:
שתעזרו לי למצוא את המילים,
ושתגידו אותן איתי, בשקט.

החול נגמר
הדינוזאור חוזר אליי.
והחבר? הוא כבר משחק במשאית אחרת.
אני מסתכל עליו,
ומושיט לו את הדינוזאור לרגע.

לפני שהחבר בא שוב
אנחנו מדברים על זה על הספה.
״איך היה לך אצלו, אם אסור לגעת?״
מה יעזור לי:
לבחור ביחד צעצוע אחד שנשאר בארון.

sources.quote: Three-year-olds are able to work out solutions to disputes by taking turns or trading toys. However, particularly in the beginning, you'll need to encourage this cooperation. ... Say to your child "use your words" to deal with problems instead of acting out. ... Remind them that when two children are sharing a toy, each gets an equal turn. ... Suggest ways to reach a simple solution when your child and another child want the same toy. They might draw for the first turn, for example, or find another toy or activity. ... Help your child with the appropriate words to describe their feelings and desires so that they don't feel frustrated.

sources.title: Getting Preschoolers to Share…How Do You Do It?
sources.publisher: Pathways.org (pediatric therapists' nonprofit, last updated 18 Jul 2025)
sources.quote: In preschool years, children are still learning how to share, so it is okay if your child isn’t great at this skill yet. ... If your child has a toy that is their absolute favorite that they do not want to share, put it away before the play date!
